channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan Strengthens Regulations on Alcohol Sales and Online Trade
item.description: Kazakhstan is tightening rules for selling alcoholic products and online trade. The Interior Ministry reported a decrease in drunk-related offenses, while police have intercepted numerous violations of alcohol sales regulations.

item.title: Uzbekistan Enhances Pediatric Oncology Drug Supply Mechanisms
item.description: Uzbekistan is improving its system for supplying vital medicines for pediatric oncology. A training in Tashkent, organized with WHO and St. Jude Children's Research Hospital, focused on scientifically forecasting drug needs and managing stock.

item.title: Kazakhstan and China to Jointly Ensure Security in Khorgos Area
item.description: Kazakhstan and China will cooperate to maintain order and security in the Khorgos area under a new agreement. The deal outlines procedures for handling suspects crossing the border and joint actions during emergencies. Kazakhstan's Interior Ministry drafted a bill to regulate this cooperation.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Russia Deepen Economic Cooperation within CIS Framework
item.description: Uzbekistan and Russia are key economic partners within the CIS, focusing on trade, industrial cooperation, energy, and interregional ties. Cooperation occurs bilaterally through an intergovernmental commission and multilaterally within the CIS and EAEU. Uzbekistan holds observer status at the EAEU.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Economy Surpasses Portugal and Finland in Size
item.description: Kazakhstan has risen to 47th globally in economic size, overtaking Portugal and Finland. The IMF projects its nominal GDP to reach nearly $398 billion by the end of 2026. Kazakhstan's economy is growing faster than the global average, with a projected real GDP growth of 4.4% for 2026.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Transition State Vehicle Fleet to Electric Cars
item.description: Kyrgyzstan plans to convert its state-owned vehicle fleet to electric vehicles. This initiative aims to modernize the government's transportation and potentially reduce environmental impact.

item.title: HIV epidemic reaches epidemic level in 27 Russian regions, raising concerns for Kazakhstan
item.description: An HIV epidemic has reached epidemic levels in 27 Russian regions, with over 1% of pregnant women infected. In Kazakhstan, 36,767 people were registered with HIV status as of early 2025. Experts explain that an epidemic means the virus is spreading among the general population, not just risk groups. Over 3% of Russian men aged 40-50 are infected.

item.title: Kazakhstan Taxpayers Reminded of November Payment Deadlines and Declarations
item.description: Kazakhstan's taxpayers must submit several declarations and pay taxes and mandatory payments in November. The State Revenue Department of Almaty has reminded taxpayers of their obligations. Most reporting is related to the third quarter results. Key deadlines include November 16 for various corporate income tax, personal income tax, VAT, and other tax declarations.

item.title: UN Women Executive Director: Women are key to lasting peace and security
item.description: Sima Bahous, Executive Director of UN Women, stated that placing women at the center of peacebuilding makes agreements more durable and strengthens resilience. She emphasized that women's leadership and security are essential for national and international security, calling for investment in women, peace, and security.

item.title: Dollar Strengthens Against Tenge on Kazakhstan Stock Exchange
item.description: The dollar's exchange rate increased by 3.52 tenge on the Kazakhstan Stock Exchange (KASE), with the average US currency rate reaching 455.63 tenge. The National Bank's official rate stands at 451.05 tenge. Exchange rates vary across different exchange points in Astana and Almaty for dollars, euros, and rubles.

item.title: Kazakhstan Banks Consider Mortgages for Individuals Without Official Income Proof
item.description: Several banks in Kazakhstan are willing to consider mortgage applications from individuals lacking official income statements. Applicants may need a substantial down payment of 40-50% or alternative proof of income. Banks like Bank CenterCredit, Altyn Bank, ForteBank, and Bank RBK are offering options, requiring bank statements or other financial documents.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Liquidates 57 Companies Due to Sanctions Risks
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is liquidating 57 companies and has closed over 240 bank accounts to minimize sanctions risks. This measure aims to prevent the country's financial infrastructure from being used to circumvent international sanctions, particularly concerning the A7 network and A7A5 stablecoin. Preventive actions have been taken against market participants linked to these entities.

item.title: Kazakhstan May Change Social Assistance Procedures
item.description: Kazakhstan is considering streamlining and consolidating individual social support measures at the local level. The digital family map will be used to assess household needs, aiming to optimize social assistance mechanisms and reduce redundant procedures. Specific details and payment lists are being finalized.

item.title: Fitch Ratings affirms Uzbekhydroenergo's creditworthiness at 'BB-'
item.description: Fitch Ratings has affirmed Uzbekhydroenergo's long-term issuer default rating at 'BB-' with a 'Stable' outlook. The agency also affirmed the company's standalone credit profile at 'b+'. Key strengths highlighted include asset quality, funding access, short-term obligation fulfillment, and financial flexibility.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev to Visit Turkey for Official Talks and Summit
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev will visit Turkey from October 28-30 at the invitation of President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan. The visit includes official talks in Ankara aimed at strengthening strategic partnership and participation in the 13th Summit of the Organization of Turkic States.

item.title: Tajikistan Citizen Travel to Russia Decreases by 40%, Over 6,500 Deported
item.description: Travel by Tajik citizens to Russia has fallen by approximately 40%. In the last 10 days in Moscow, over 6,500 migrants have been ordered for deportation. The article provides further details on this situation.

item.title: Kazakhstan Expands Search for Alimony Debtors' Income Sources
item.description: Kazakhstan will broaden the automatic search for alimony debtors' income, including from taxi services, delivery, and gambling. Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov announced that bailiffs can now request information from online platforms and gambling organizers. This aims to improve support for families not receiving alimony.

item.title: Uzbek Labor Migration to Russia Falls 13.2% in First Half of 2026
item.description: Uzbek citizens made the most work-related entries into Russia, despite a 13.2% decline compared to the previous year. TASS reported 1,178,609 such entries. Remittances from Russia to Uzbekistan increased by 8.8% in the same period, though declining migration poses a potential risk to household income.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's BARS Electric Vehicle Plant Opening Delayed to Late 2026 or Spring 2027
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's BARS electric vehicle assembly plant has missed its September opening date. Production is now expected in late 2026 or spring 2027, according to President Sadyr Japarov. The plant aims to produce 10,000 vehicles annually, initially using imported components, with plans for local manufacturing later.

item.title: Kazakhstan Plans 8.5% Pension Increase Effective January 2027
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to increase pension payments by 8.5% starting January 1, 2027. The draft budget outlines a minimum cumulative pension of 113,541 tenge and a maximum of 259,795 tenge. Final payment amounts are subject to budget review and depend on individual work history and previous earnings.

item.title: Former Prisoners in Turkmenistan Denied Tuberculosis Treatment
item.description: Residents of Turkmenabat report that former prisoners diagnosed with tuberculosis are being denied admission to local hospitals. Sources indicate a high prevalence of the disease among those released in the last three years, with some contracting it in prison and others diagnosed post-release.

item.title: Kazakhstan Reports Lower Tax Revenue from Self-Employed in Mangystau and West Kazakhstan
item.description: Tax revenues from the simplified declaration regime for self-employed individuals have decreased in the Mangystau and West Kazakhstan regions. While the regime remains for small businesses, with increased income limits and no employee caps, its contribution to state revenue in these areas has fallen.

item.title: President Tokayev to Visit Turkey for Official Talks and Turkic States Summit
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev will undertake an official visit to Turkey from October 28-30 at the invitation of President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan. Discussions will focus on strengthening the strategic partnership. Tokayev will also attend the 13th Summit of the Organization of Turkic States.

item.title: UN Women Official Warns of World's Most Severe Women's Rights Crisis in Afghanistan
item.description: Nyaradzayi Gumbonzvanda of UN Women stated that Afghanistan faces the world's most severe women's rights crisis, with girls denied education. She highlighted the need for women's inclusion in peace processes and decision-making, noting over 37,000 civilian deaths last year, a quarter being women and girls.

item.title: Kazakhstan: 'Adil Soz' Foundation Reports Facebook Page Blocked Within Country
item.description: The 'Adil Soz' Foundation, advocating for freedom of speech, announced its Facebook page has been blocked within Kazakhstan. The foundation believes the social media administrator cited copyright infringement as the reason. They have appealed to Meta, Facebook's parent company, for a detailed explanation and to unblock the page.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Bailiffs Can Now Request Alimony Debtor Information from Taxi and Delivery Services
item.description: In Kazakhstan, bailiffs have gained the authority to request alimony debtor income information from online platforms, including taxi and delivery services, and gambling organizers. This expansion of powers aims to improve the collection of child support payments by accessing data on employment, earnings, and other income sources, including those from digital platforms.

item.title: Tajikistan and US Discuss Cooperation on Combating Human Trafficking
item.description: On October 26, 2026, Tajikistan's Interior Ministry hosted a meeting between the Deputy Interior Minister and representatives from the US and the International Organization for Migration. Discussions focused on strengthening cooperation against human trafficking and aiding victims. Professional development for relevant government officials was also addressed, alongside modern threats like terrorism and organized crime.

item.title: Tajikistan Signs Labor Migration Agreement with Belarus, Offering Jobs Up to $1200 Monthly
item.description: Tajikistan's Foreign Labor Migration Agency has signed agreements with over 10 employers in Belarus's Grodno region. Tajik citizens can find work in construction, agriculture, textiles, manufacturing, heavy industry, services, and transport. Salaries range from $750 to $1200, with employers providing accommodation and partial meals. Russian language proficiency, a clean criminal record, and good health are required.

item.title: Kazakhstan Delivers Message to Saudi Crown Prince, Discusses Regional Issues
item.description: Kazakhstan's Deputy Foreign Minister Arman Issagaliyev met with Saudi Arabia's First Deputy Foreign Minister Waleed Al-Khuraiji. Issagaliyev conveyed a written message from President Tokayev to Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, expressing solidarity and support for Saudi security efforts. The officials exchanged views on regional situations and bilateral relations.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Plans to Increase Protected Natural Areas to 30% by 2035
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is developing a strategy to expand protected natural areas, aiming to cover 30% of the country's territory by 2035. This initiative includes protecting high-altitude glaciers, mountain areas, and state forests, while allowing traditional grazing in buffer zones.

item.title: Germany to Fund Water Supply Improvement for 27 Border Villages in Batken
item.description: Germany will provide financial support to improve drinking and irrigation water supply in 27 border villages in Kyrgyzstan's Batken region. The project, funded by the German government, aims to enhance agricultural conditions and ensure stable water access for residents.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Collect Alimony Debts from Taxi, Delivery, and Betting Incomes
item.description: In Kazakhstan, taxi services, delivery companies, and betting platforms will be required to withhold income from individuals who are in arrears with alimony payments. This measure aims to ensure that child support obligations are met by accessing funds from these specific income sources. The new regulations are expected to improve the collection of overdue alimony.

item.title: Uzbekistan Discusses Application of Insolvency Legislation at Supreme Court Roundtable
item.description: A roundtable discussion on the application of insolvency legislation was held at the Supreme Court of Uzbekistan, involving specialized judges, representatives from the Asian Development Bank, and the Konrad Adenauer Foundation. The event aimed to foster professional dialogue and develop unified approaches to resolving issues arising in judicial practice concerning insolvency, crucial for business entities, creditors, and the overall business environment.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Bans Apple Imports Until February 2027 to Support Local Growers
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has prohibited the import of apples from other countries until February 1, 2027. The decision by the Cabinet of Ministers aims to support domestic producers and ensure the sale of local harvests. The Ministry of Agriculture plans to organize local fairs and control prices, while also preparing a thousand-day reform program for the agricultural sector.

item.title: Iran, Pakistan, Turkey, Saudi Arabia Hold Talks to Reduce Regional Tensions
item.description: Representatives from Iran, Pakistan, Turkey, and Saudi Arabia met in Tehran to discuss regional security and diplomatic efforts to resolve crises. The meeting, initiated by Islamabad, focused on regional security, the consequences of military aggression, and aid for Palestine and Lebanon. Saudi Arabia's Defense Minister attended, emphasizing dialogue and diplomatic solutions.

item.title: Anti-Terrorism Drills 'Batken-Antiterror—2026' Held in Kadamdzhai
item.description: Anti-terrorism drills codenamed 'Batken-Antiterror—2026' were conducted in Kadamdzhai, according to the State Committee for National Security. The exercises involved establishing a regional operational headquarters, practicing the detection, blocking, and neutralization of terrorist groups, and assessing the security of strategic sites.

item.title: Afghanistan's Economy Minister and UNDP Representative Discuss Development Cooperation
item.description: Afghanistan's Economy Minister, Din Mohammad Hanif, met with UNDP Resident Representative Turhan Saleh to discuss expanding development cooperation. The minister cited sanctions and frozen reserves as hindering economic development, while highlighting efforts in domestic production and water management. The UNDP reaffirmed its commitment to continued cooperation.

item.title: Tajikistan Sets Minimum Age of 18 for Labor Migrants
item.description: Tajik citizens can now only leave the country for work if they are 18 years or older, according to a new law on migration. The law, published on October 23, also stipulates that labor migration is permitted only to countries that ensure the protection of migrants' rights. This age restriction also applies to foreign citizens coming to work in Tajikistan.

item.title: Construction of Artificial Reservoir Begins in Nurata District, Uzbekistan
item.description: Construction of an artificial reservoir has commenced in the Jarma mahalla of Nurata district, Navoi region, Uzbekistan. The project aims to increase water reserves and improve water resource efficiency. Implemented under a presidential decree, the 3.3 billion soum project will help address water supply issues, ensure stable irrigation, and restore groundwater levels.

item.title: Taliban Unable to Stop Extortion and Kidnapping by Noorzai's Nephew
item.description: Haji Bashir Noorzai's nephew, known as Safir Almas or Almas Noorzai, is reportedly extorting wealthy individuals and businessmen in Afghanistan. Sources claim he demands protection money, kidnaps relatives, and threatens death to those who refuse. The Taliban's security and intelligence agencies admit they cannot stop him, advising victims to resolve issues themselves.
